Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg., cor EDSA Mapagmahal Street, Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. 18 S. 2010 March 03, 2010 MARILOU B. GESLANI Municipal Local Government Operations Officer Malasiqui, Pangasinan Dear Ms. Geslani: This pertains to your letter requesting this Department's legal opinion on the following queries, which we quote: "A) One of the Barangay Members of Barangay Poblacion resigned on February 16, 2009. According to source, the person to be recommended by the Barangay Council is the son of the Mayor and please be informed also that the Punong Barangay of said barangay is the son also of the Mayor. My question is, can the Mayor appoint his son to replace the vacated position in the Sangguniang Barangay? Is it not covered by nepotism? B) One of the members of the Sangguniang Barangay of Barangay Payar resigned on December 31, 2009. The Sangguniang Barangay then recommended Mr. Samuel Macaraeg and submitted their resolution sometime in January to the Municipal Mayor. The Mayor did not act on the recommendation of the Barangay Council. It is specified in the Local Govemment Code of 1991 that there should be no vacant position jn the Sanggunian. What will the Barangay Council do with the situated stated above?" In reply to your first query, please be informed that "Nepotism" has been defined by the Civil Setvice Law as bestowal of patronage by public officers in appointing others to positions by reason of blood or marital relationships to the appointing authority. This is prohibited by law and the prohibition has been reiterated in the Local Govemment Code with respect to appointments of local officials and employees. Thus, Section 79 of the Local Govemment Code provides and we therefore quote: "No person shall be appointed in the career service of the local govemment if he is related within the fourth civil degree of consanguinity or affinity to the appointing authority." The above-quoted provision of the law on nepotism expressly and clearly applies only to positions in the career service. Under the Civil Service Law, elective officials are considered and embraced in the non-career service. A Sangguniang Barangay Member is an elective position, therefore being an elective position it will not be covered by the law on nepotism.
